yaml.load() is called with Loader=yaml.Loader (the unsafe/full loader) on user-supplied YAML input from request.get_json()['profile_yaml']. This allows arbitrary Python object deserialization, enabling remote code execution. An attacker can craft a YAML payload with !!python/object/apply: directives to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

The update_password endpoint takes user_id from the request body (data.get('user_id')) instead of using current_user.id, allowing any authenticated user to change any other user's password. There is no authorization check to verify that the requesting user is changing their own password or has admin privileges.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: MD5 is used to hash passwords in the set_password method. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing: it is fast to compute, vulnerable to collision attacks, and susceptible to rainbow table attacks. Should use bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2.

MD5 is used to verify passwords in the check_password method. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing. Should use a constant-time comparison with bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 to also prevent timing attacks.
MD5 is used to hash the password in the register endpoint, duplicating the weak hashing from the User model. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing.

The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'supersecret'. This key is used for signing session cookies and other security-sensitive operations. An attacker who discovers this key can forge session cookies and potentially escalate privileges.
The JWT signing secret is hardcoded as 'secret' when encoding tokens. An attacker who discovers this key can forge valid JWT tokens for any user, completely bypassing authentication.
The JWT verification secret is hardcoded as 'secret' when decoding tokens. This same secret is used for encoding, and its exposure allows token forgery for any user.

The CORS after_request handler reflects the request's Origin header back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests, effectively nullifying the same-origin policy. An attacker can steal authenticated user data from any malicious website.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Flask debug mode is enabled (debug=True) and the server is bound to all interfaces (host='0.0.0.0'). Debug mode exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which allows arbitrary code execution via the browser. Binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes this to all network interfaces.

Social Security Numbers (SSNs) are stored in plaintext in the user profile JSON field. SSNs are highly sensitive PII and should be encrypted at rest. extra.message: The balance check (line 30) and balance deduction (lines 33-34) are not atomic operations. Combined with the autocommit isolation level set in app.py:23, concurrent transfer requests can pass the balance check simultaneously, allowing an account to be overdrawn. This is a TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) race condition in a financial transaction.

SQLite isolation_level is set to None (autocommit mode), disabling transaction-based atomicity. In a banking application, this means database operations are not atomic — partial updates can persist on failure, and race conditions in balance transfers become exploitable.
